citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The licensee is not currently using appropriate methods to treat an eye condition. The left of eye of dog #13 appeared
cloudy on the surface with a brownish-red centralized area and reddened sclera. There is an oily, silvery substance in the
hair around the eye. The licensee was treating this eye with neomycin ophthalmic ointment once daily last week, but ran
out. He then switched to using two different topical wound treatments, an M&J Wonder Healing solution and a Vetericyn
umbilical and navel wound spray on the eye. Neither of these latter products are included in the program of veterinary
care's instructions for eye problems. Inspectors contacted the attending veterinarian and described the current treatments
(M&J and Vetericyn), which the attending veterinarian did not believe were appropriate methods to treat the eye condition
as described.
Using methods other than those prescribed by the attending veterinarian, or as written in the program of veterinary care,
to treat conditions can actually cause more harm and are not consistent with adequate veterinary care.
Correct by using appropriate methods, including only those prescribed or as written in the program of veterinary care by
the attending veterinarian, to prevent, diagnose, control, and treat diseases and injuries.
Correct beginning 7/30/26.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not have an effective pest control program in place to control flying insects in the kennel. Inspectors
observed excessive numbers of insects flying/landing on the floor, walls, and dishes in the kennel housing 9 adult dogs
and 8 puppies. The facility did have multiple large fly tapes hanging in the facility. However, the fly tapes were no longer
effective due to the number of insects already attached. Failure to ensure that an effective pest control program is in place
can lead to disease spread and stress in the animals. The facility must establish and maintain an effective program for the
control of insects, external parasites affecting dogs and cats, and birds and mammals that are pests so as to promote the
health and well-being of the animals and reduce contamination by pests in animal areas. Correct by, 03-August-2026.

The licensee did not make a medical record for the treatments he used for an eye condition. Dog #13 had an eye
condition the licensee stated began last week and he initiated treatments, but did not make an appropriate medical record
of the problem, names, and dates of treatments given. Complete medical records are necessary to ensure dogs have
received appropriate care.
Correct by making medical records for any problems identified that include the dog's identification, a description of the
problem, the date identified, the results of any examinations or testing, and the names and dates of all treatments given.
Correct starting 7/30/26.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a Facility Representative.
Additional Inspectors:
KATHRYN CAMPITELLI, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
